blocks.value: Generics let you write one class or method that works with any type, instead of duplicating the same code for each type you need to support. A type parameter, written in angle brackets, acts as a placeholder for whatever real type gets used when the class is actually created.

T here is just a name; any valid identifier would work, but single capital letters are the convention: E for Element, K for Key, N for Number, T for Type, V for Value. Wherever T appears inside the class (as the type of data, the parameter of setValue, the return type of getValue), it all resolves to whatever concrete type is supplied when the object is created.

getClass() (defined on every object via Object) returns a Class object representing the object's actual runtime type; getName() on that Class object returns its name as a String, which is how showType() can report what T turned out to be.
